- Self-Consistency: a universe where temporal contradictions are excluded (time and causality, loop).

sourceText: cells: Bs, Ac The BOOTSTRAP-PATENT-OFFICE sector was already in progress when they entered. For several lessons Aster had refused to pause worlds for their arrival; the fact that a class was visiting was not a cosmic event for the inhabitants. A device is built from plans sent from the future, and those same plans are later sent back, with no originating author. The memorial bore the name of causal-loop traditions precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. Aster could follow many histories at once. That very capacity made the lesson difficult: for her, an alternative was almost an object; for the inhabitants of worlds, it was what had not happened. Orin perceived counterfactual costs as absences with weight. He did not confuse an unrealized branch with a victim, but he refused to let success rewrite rejected options as if they had been inevitable all along. The children were met by Sael, who refused demonstrations. ‘If you can perform miracles, perform them after you tell me what becomes irreversible.’ Marae appreciated the formulation; Aster 127 admitted that in earlier eras she herself would have asked the question only after optimizing. The problem closed quickly around them: When defects appear, no one knows who has the right to modify a design whose existence depends on fidelity to itself. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Bs — Causal Bootstrap: information exists without a clear external origin; Ac — Self-Consistency: temporal contradictions are excluded. Course references included causal-loop fiction; self-consistent time travel. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Marae broke the first consensus. ‘Do not tell me what their model prefers. Ask them, and bear the time their answer takes.’ Vela answered without raising their voice: ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. For Aster, the pain came not from too few worlds but from the fact that too many had become transparent. She could build 128 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS variations faster than a human could formulate desires, but calculated variation did not produce exteriority. It was like trying to surprise yourself by moving objects around your own room with your eyes closed. Vela evaluated the solution not by efficiency but by the differences it made invisible. She found one: a local minority for whom the proposed “improvement” destroyed a practice with no equivalent. Optimizing the average concealed a small and perfectly legal extinction. The night did not end in victory. For an instant Aster encounters an idea with no attributable origin, and the Hunger drops violently. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. While Kesh closed the record, Tern compared the sector’s noise with the anomaly detected in the Vinge zone. The pattern reappeared, but only in worlds where Aster’s control weakened. The correlation was unpleasant: either someone was calling him from outside, or his own need for an outside was learning to forge evidence. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the COPYING operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — creates a second instance similar enough for continuity to become a problem — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a 129 copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. When the threshold closed, Aster remained silent one second longer than protocol required. The children had already noticed that this was her smallest unit of fear. 130 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
